newsitem.title: USA: IMM yen seen nearing long-term retracement level.
newsitem.headline: IMM yen seen nearing long-term retracement level.

text.p: IMM March yen futures skidded through support to hit a series of fresh contract lows today and appear to be headed near a long-term retracement level, technicians said.
The midpoint of the range from the past 15 years is at $0.008110 in March yen, with the middle of the dollar/yen's range during the same time at 179.01.

A variety of fundamental and technical woes have slammed yen futures to the lowest level on monthly continuation charts since early 1993. March yen reached a new contract low of $0.008266 this afternoon, but recovered slightly to $0.008294 at 1342 CST/1942 GMT.
Tim Ransford, technician with Dean Witter Reynolds in Chicago, pegged support at $0.008250 to $0.008300 and at $0.008125.

Below those levels lies $0.008110 -- the midpoint of the contract's 15 year range, Ransford noted. The yen futures contract -- on a monthly continuous basis -- in November 1982 dipped to $0.003596. By April 1995 it had climbed to a peak of $0.012625 before spending the next 21 months in a downtrend on monthly charts, Ransford said.
"I think $0.008250 to $0.008300 stands an excellent chance for any potential for a recovery," Ransford said. "A positive reaction within those 50 ticks could trigger a decisive recovery attempt."
"I think it could be the difference between them actually crushing it to $0.007800 or worse, or correcting."
The 62 percent retracement of that 15-year range is $0.007045, and $0.009176 was the 38 percent retracement, technicians said.
But Peter McTeague, technical market strategist at MCM TradeWatch in Boston, said the move in yen futures was starting to accelerate.
"In the bigger scheme of things, I'm not sure if ($0.008110 in futures) is going to stop the train," McTeague said. He said dollar/yen appeared on track for more gains.

"There's still a way to go in the spot retracements," McTeague said. He noted the 50 percent retracement of roughly the same 15-year range in the interbank market was 179.01 yen. That range saw dollar/yen peak at 278.24 yen in November 1982 and descend to 79.78 by April 1995, he said.
The 38 percent retracement of that move is 155.59, McTeague said.
The $0.008110 area could be a mild downside futures target, McTeague said, but "the market will gravitate toward the spot levels," McTeague said.
